acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Host Ira Glass talks to B.A. Parker about her birthday tradition.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: Producer Aviva DeKornfeld speaks with a father and daughter who have been playing the same game for 25 years.
acts.title: Will You Still Slug Me Tomorrow?

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
Talia Augustidis asks a single question over and over.
A version of this story originally aired on Short Cuts, a Falling Tree production for BBC Radio 4.
acts.title: I’ll Repeat the Question

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc:
Editor David Kestenbaum speaks with Jeff Permar, who is trapped in a Groundhog Day situation — with an actual groundhog!
See more videos of the groundhog Chunk on Jeff’s YouTube channel.
acts.title: Raiders of the Lost Chard

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Parking in a big city can be a real pain. Producer Valerie Kipnis speaks with a man who has taken it upon himself to try to mitigate the weekly hassle.
acts.title: Heart of Parkness

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc:
Short fiction from Bess Kalb about a groundhog named Susan, who has her own opinions about the holiday named after her species.
You can find more work from Bess at The Grudge Report on Substack.
acts.credits: By Bess Kalb; Produced by Bim Adewunmi and Aviva DeKornfeld

songs.a: Richard Thompson & “Punxsutawney Rock” by Tari Kelly & Tim Minchin (radio only)

acts.title: It's Been a Hard Year's Night, and I've Been Working Like a Hog
